030package dev.visdb.seesaw.datasources;
031
032import java.sql.Connection;
033import java.sql.DatabaseMetaData;
034import java.sql.SQLException;
035
036import dev.visdb.seesaw.utils.SsUtils;
037
038/**
039 * Metadata cache. Only static and Driver info, capabilities, and limits should
040 * be referenced. Information that is subject to change as the database is
041 * running should not be referenced.
042 * <p>
043 * <b>NOTE:</b> There's only one database, found in SsUtils.dbSupport.getSharedConnection.
044 *
045 */
046public class DbMetaDataCache {
047  private DbMetaDataCache() {}
048
049  //
050  // The databasemetadata is cached, so only the first call connects to
051  // the database. Note: some information is not necessarily safe to cache;
052  // google search: "with jdbc is it safe to cache databasemetadata"
053  //
054  // Make this a selective cache. In particular Static/Driver info,
055  // capabilities/Limits. But not tables & Column details.
056  // Then no worry about needing to flush in some cases.
057  //
058  // TODO: this class could provide methods that are "safe", with exactly
059  //       the same names as used in DatabaseMetaData, and return this
060  //       rather than the metadata itself. Then there would be no chance
061  //       of referencing non-cachable data.
062  //
063
064  private static DatabaseMetaData metaData;
065
066  // TODO: flush/refresh/enable, other maintenance methods?
067  // All accesses to metadata could go through here by adding
068  // a "refresh" flag. Is that useful or confusing?
069
070  /**
071   * @return the MetaData cache for the default database from getSharedConnection().
072   * @throws java.sql.SQLException
073   */
074  public static DatabaseMetaData get() throws SQLException {
075    if (metaData == null) {
076      Connection shconn = SsUtils.dbSupport().getSharedConnection();
077      if (shconn == null)
078        return null;
079      metaData = shconn.getMetaData();
080    }
081    return metaData;
082  }
083}
